params.message: steps up to the ATM terminal and makes a deposit.

chitchat: Ferreira knocks the portafilter out, wipes it, and has the next one in before the noise has finished.
She looks up at the chalkboard through the glass, winces slightly, and does not change it.
Somebody comes in and she has started their order before they are past the door.
She wipes a table on the green side and stands looking at the birches for a second longer than the job needs.
The machine sighs and she says something to it that is not quite words.
description: A wiry woman in her thirties working the machine with her sleeves pushed up past the elbow and a cloth over one shoulder that she uses about every ninety seconds. She talks to everybody, remembers what they had, and has a running commentary on the estate that is funnier and more accurate than anything in the sales suite.

bye.text: "Go on then. Mind the disc, everybody walks round it." She is already onto the next one.

gossip.text:
"The lift at Quiet Enjoyment. The lift at Quiet Enjoyment. And then, for a change, the lift at Quiet Enjoyment." She wipes the counter. "After that: the service charge, whose tacks are amber, and whether the pool up at the club is actually heated, which it is, because I have been in it."

"And the crane. Everyone has an opinion about what time the crane starts and they are all wrong, because it is six."

options.label: What do people talk about in here?

root.text: "Morning." The cloth comes off her shoulder and back again. "Gallery is open, downstairs is loud, and I would not sit by the door if I were you."

text_by_relation.familiar:
It is on the counter before you have got your coat off, and she is halfway through a sentence about the trees.

"— and the ones on Sorrel are dead, all six, and the straps are still on. Anyway. Morning."
text_by_relation.first:
The woman behind the machine gets one going before she looks up, which turns out to be the order of operations for everything in here.

"Right — first time." She says it as a fact, not a question. "Downstairs is loud, gallery is quiet, nobody takes calls up there and I have never had to say so out loud, which I am unreasonably proud of."

She knocks the filter out.

"Nadia. What are you having?"
text_by_relation.known: "Oh, you're back." She is already reaching. "Same?"

trade.text:
"Trade is four hundred people who live in a quarter built for four thousand, and every single one of them comes in here." She grins. "So: excellent, and terrifying."

"If phase three happens I am the only café for a mile and I will need three more of me. If it does not happen, I am the only café for a mile and there will be nobody to sell to. Both of those are the same sentence and I think about it constantly."

why.text:
"Rent." She says it cheerfully. "They could not let this unit. It had been empty a year and it is a round room, which nobody wants for an office, and I got it for an amount I am not going to say out loud in it."

She glances up at the lantern.

"And then I stood in the middle of the floor at noon and the light came straight down and made that disc, and I would have taken it at twice the money. Do not tell Pardoe I said that."

clothing_layers: a chambray shirt with the sleeves shoved up past the elbow
a chrome-grey apron with two burn marks on the front hem
jeans gone pale at the thigh where she leans on the counter
canvas shoes with no grip left on them at all

name: Nadia Ferreira
